examples.en: I heard that proactivity is important in interviews.
The teacher praised the students' proactivity.

examples.ko: 팀에서 적극성만 있다고 일이 잘되는 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Having proactivity alone doesn't make work go well in a team.
Proactivity is needed, but consideration matters too.
Everyone was surprised by his drive.

examples.ko: 동생은 적극성이 부족해서 손을 잘 안 들어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling lacks initiative and rarely raises a hand.

explain: '적극성이 있다/없다/부족하다'처럼 말하고, 반대말은 '소극성'이에요. 사람을 직접 설명할 때는 '적극적이다'가 더 자주 쓰여요. 면접, 수업, 회사 이야기에서 칭찬이나 아쉬운 점을 말할 때 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: The new employee is proactive about work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 성격이나 태도를 직접 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a person's character or attitude directly.

phrases.en: That student shows enthusiasm in class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행동으로 드러난 태도를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the attitude shows in actions.

phrases.example: 제가 발표할 때 적극성이 부족하다는 말을 들었어요.
phrases.en: I was told that I lack enthusiasm when I present.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아쉬운 점을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to point out a shortcoming.

explain_en: You say '적극성이 있다/없다/부족하다', and the opposite is '소극성'. To describe a person directly, '적극적이다' is used more often. It comes up in interviews, classes and the workplace when praising someone or noting a shortcoming.

en: to be enormous; to be great; to be considerable

examples.ko: 스승의 가르침은 제 인생에 지대한 영향을 줬어요.
examples.en: My teacher's lessons had an immense influence on my life.

examples.ko: 그 소식에 대한 사람들의 관심이 지대했어요.
examples.en: People's interest in that news was huge.

examples.ko: 이 사고가 지역 경제에 끼칠 피해가 지대할 거예요.
examples.en: The damage this accident will do to the local economy will be great.
Parents play a hugely important role in a child's growth.
His contribution is immense, and everyone acknowledges it.

examples.ko: 그 발명이 사회에 미친 영향이 얼마나 지대했는지 몰라요.
examples.en: You can't imagine how great the invention's impact on society was.

explain: '지대하다'는 영향·관심·공처럼 눈에 안 보이는 것이 아주 클 때만 써요. 물건이나 건물의 크기에는 '크다'를 써요. 뉴스나 글에서 '지대한 영향', '지대한 관심'으로 굳어서 나오고, 말할 때는 '아주 크다', '엄청나다'가 더 많이 들려요.

phrases.example: 부모의 말은 아이에게 지대한 영향을 줘요.
phrases.en: Parents' words have a great influence on a child.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이고 주로 글에서 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, mostly seen in writing.

phrases.example: 많은 사람이 그 일에 지대한 관심을 보여요.
phrases.en: Many people show great interest in that matter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 관심이 아주 클 때 '지대한 관심'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Say 지대한 관심 when interest is very great.

phrases.example: 그 일이 저에게 미친 영향은 아주 커요.
phrases.en: The effect that had on me is very big.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때는 '아주 크다'가 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: 아주 크다 sounds more natural in speech.

explain_en: Formal, written: used for abstract things like influence or interest (영향이 지대하다) 지대하다 is used only for things you can't see, such as influence, interest, or contribution. For physical size, use 크다. It appears mostly as set phrases like 지대한 영향 and 지대한 관심 in news and writing; in speech, people say 아주 크다 or 엄청나다.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 품성이 따뜻해서 모두가 좋아해요.
examples.en: He has a warm character, so everyone likes him.

examples.ko: 아이의 품성은 가정 교육에서 많이 길러져요.
examples.en: A child's character is largely shaped by upbringing at home.

examples.ko: 좋은 품성을 가진 사람과 일하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to work with people of good character.
I heard interviewers look closely at an applicant's character too.
Thanks to his excellent character, he even received an award.
There is nothing to criticize about his character.

explain: '성격'은 밝다, 급하다처럼 타고난 기질까지 두루 말하지만, '품성'은 사람 됨됨이, 곧 인품과 도덕적인 면을 말할 때 써요. 그래서 '품성이 좋다, 바르다'처럼 칭찬하는 문장에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 좋은 품성을 가진 사람이 되고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I want to be a person of good character.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바람직한 사람 됨됨이를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for desirable personal character.

phrases.en: That student was praised for having upright character.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예의 바르고 도덕적인 사람을 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Praises someone who is polite and moral.

phrases.example: 책을 읽으면 품성을 기를 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Reading can help you build character.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교육이나 경험으로 길러 간다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Suggests developing character through education or experience.

explain_en: '성격' covers temperament in general, such as cheerful or hasty, but '품성' is about a person's moral character and quality. That is why it often appears in praise like '품성이 좋다' or '품성이 바르다'.

en: to be boundless; to be endless; to be limitless

examples.en: The love my parents gave me is truly boundless.
I don't know how to repay my endless gratitude.
I was endlessly happy when I heard I passed.
She comforted the child with an infinitely gentle voice.

examples.ko: 그 말을 들으니 제 자신이 한없이 작아졌어요.
examples.en: Hearing those words, I felt infinitely small.

examples.ko: 한없던 슬픔도 시간이 지나니 조금씩 줄었어요.
examples.en: Even my endless sadness slowly lessened as time passed.

explain: '끝없다'는 길, 바다처럼 눈에 보이는 것에도 많이 쓰고, '한없다'는 사랑, 기쁨, 슬픔 같은 마음에 자주 써요. 대부분 '한없이' 꼴로 나오고, '한없는 사랑'처럼 꾸밀 때는 '한없는'을 써요.

phrases.en: I was endlessly happy to hear I passed.
phrases.nuance_ko: '한없이'는 형용사 앞에 붙어 마음이 끝이 없이 크다는 뜻을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: 한없이 before an adjective adds a sense of boundless feeling.

phrases.en: I'm endlessly grateful for your help.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고마움이 매우 크다는 걸 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to express very deep gratitude.

phrases.en: The endlessly stretching sea was beautiful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈에 보이는 길이나 바다에도 쓸 수 있어서 '한없다'보다 넓게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can also be used for visible things like roads or the sea, so it is broader than 한없다.

explain_en: '끝없다' is often used for visible things like roads or the sea, while '한없다' is often used for feelings such as love, joy and sadness. It mostly appears as '한없이', and '한없는' is used to modify a noun, as in '한없는 사랑' (boundless love).

en: to be bright; to be innocent; to be clear

examples.en: The child's smile is truly bright and innocent.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 늘 해맑은 얼굴로 인사해요.
examples.en: That child always greets people with a bright, innocent face.

examples.ko: 해맑게 웃는 모습을 보면 기분이 좋아져요.
examples.en: Seeing her laugh so brightly makes me feel good.
Puppies are so carefree that just seeing them makes me happy.

examples.ko: 어른이 되어도 해맑은 마음을 잃고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: Even as an adult, I don't want to lose my innocent heart.

examples.ko: 그는 해맑았던 어린 시절을 가끔 떠올려요.
examples.en: He sometimes remembers his innocent childhood.

explain: '해맑다'는 얼굴이나 웃음이 맑고 순수해서 걱정이 없어 보일 때 써요. 아이나 강아지처럼 순수한 대상에 주로 쓰고, 어른에게 쓰면 철이 없다는 뜻으로 들릴 때도 있어요. '해맑게 웃다'로 가장 많이 써요.

phrases.en: The baby looked at me and smiled brightly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '해맑다'를 부사형으로 써서 웃는 모습을 꾸며요. 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form describes how someone smiles. It is the most common collocation.

phrases.example: 그 아이의 해맑은 미소에 기분이 좋아졌어요.
phrases.en: The child's pure smile made me feel good.
phrases.nuance_ko: '해맑다'를 명사 앞에 붙인 활용형이에요. 순수하고 밝은 웃음을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form before a noun, meaning a pure, bright smile.

phrases.example: 강아지가 마당에서 뛰어놀 때 해맑아 보여요.
phrases.en: The puppy looks so carefree when it plays in the yard.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 보이다'로 겉모습이 그렇게 느껴질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -아/어 보이다 it describes how something appears.

explain_en: Bright and innocent like a child, a clear unclouded look. '해맑다' describes a face or smile that is clear and pure, looking free of worries. It is used mostly for children and puppies, and for an adult it can sometimes sound like naive. The usual phrase is '해맑게 웃다'.

t90.ax: He sometimes remembers his innocent childhood.

en: to be countless; to be plenty; to be numerous

examples.en: Things like that are everywhere around us.
Plenty of people were late because of the traffic.

examples.ko: 요즘 이런 사기 전화는 허다하다고 해요.
examples.en: They say scam calls like this are everywhere these days.

examples.ko: 이 동네에는 빈 가게가 허다해서 걱정이에요.
examples.en: There are plenty of empty shops in this neighborhood, which worries me.

examples.ko: 시험에 떨어지는 경우도 허다하니까 너무 걱정하지 마세요.
examples.en: Failing an exam happens all the time, so don't worry too much.

examples.ko: 주말에는 줄을 서는 가게가 허다할 거예요.
examples.en: On weekends, there will be plenty of shops with lines.

explain: '흔하다'와 비슷하지만 '허다하다'는 글이나 뉴스, 어른의 말투에 어울리는 딱딱한 말이에요. 주로 '~는 경우가 허다하다', '~는 사람이 허다하다'처럼 수가 아주 많다고 말할 때 써요. 가벼운 대화에서는 '많아요', '흔해요'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: There are plenty of cases of being late for appointments.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그런 경우가 아주 많다고 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form for saying such cases are very numerous.

phrases.en: There are plenty of people who sleep in on weekends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그런 사람이 아주 많다고 말할 때 써요. '경우' 대신 '사람'이나 '일'을 넣어 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say there are very many such people. You can put 'person' or 'thing' in place of 'case'.

phrases.en: Nowadays that kind of thing is common.
phrases.nuance_ko: '허다하다'보다 부드럽고 일상 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Softer than 'heodahada' and more common in daily conversation.

explain_en: It is similar to '흔하다', but '허다하다' is stiffer and fits writing, news and adult speech. It is mostly used in patterns like '~는 경우가 허다하다' or '~는 사람이 허다하다' to say there are very many. In casual talk, '많아요' or '흔해요' sounds more natural.

en: to be sound; to be healthy; to be wholesome

examples.en: If you have a wholesome hobby, your stress decreases.
This game is wholesome even for children.
The habit of spending money sensibly is important.
Don't visit sites that aren't wholesome.
They say that if your body is healthy, your mind becomes sound too.

examples.ko: 회사 재정이 건전해서 오래 일하고 싶어요.
examples.en: The company's finances are sound, so I want to work there a long time.

explain: '건강하다'는 몸이나 마음의 상태가 좋을 때 쓰고, '건전하다'는 생각, 취미, 문화, 재정이 바르고 문제가 없을 때 써요. '건전한 생각', '건전 가요'처럼 쓰고, 몸이 튼튼하다는 말은 보통 '건강하다'를 써요. 반대말은 '불건전하다'예요.

phrases.en: There are many people with sound thinking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생각이 바르고 문제가 없다는 칭찬의 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A compliment meaning the thinking is proper and without problems.

phrases.en: This movie isn't wholesome for children.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내용이나 분위기가 바람직하지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when content or atmosphere is not wholesome.

phrases.en: Healthy spending habits are needed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈 쓰는 방식이 바르고 무리가 없다는 뜻으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for spending that is sensible and not excessive.

explain_en: Healthy in a moral or social sense: hobbies, culture, minds. 건강하다 is for a good state of body or mind, while 건전하다 is for thoughts, hobbies, culture, or finances that are proper and free of problems. It appears in 건전한 생각 (a sound way of thinking) and 건전 가요 (clean pop songs); for a strong body, people usually say 건강하다. The opposite is 불건전하다.

t90.ax: Don't visit sites that aren't wholesome.

examples.en: Many people hope for Korean reunification.

examples.ko: 남북통일이 되면 기차로 유럽까지 갈 수 있을까요?
examples.en: If the Koreas were reunified, could we travel to Europe by train?
We learned about Korean reunification in class today.
Our class debated the topic of Korean reunification.

examples.ko: 할머니는 남북통일을 꼭 보고 싶다고 하셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother said she really wants to see reunification.
We talked about how much reunification would cost.

explain: 뉴스나 수업에서는 '통일'이라고만 줄여 말할 때도 많아요. '통일을 하다'보다는 '통일이 되다', '통일을 이루다'처럼 말해요. 비슷한 말로 '평화통일'도 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: We talked about reunification.
phrases.nuance_ko: '남북통일'을 줄여 말할 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common short form of 남북통일.

phrases.en: If reunification happens, where do you want to go?
phrases.nuance_ko: 통일이 이루어진다는 뜻으로 '되다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses 되다 to mean that reunification takes place.

phrases.en: Many people hope for peaceful reunification.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전쟁 없이 이루는 통일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means reunification achieved without war.

explain_en: In the news and in class it is often shortened to just '통일'. People usually say '통일이 되다' or '통일을 이루다' rather than '통일을 하다'. A related term you will often see is '평화통일'.

en: to always exist; to be ever-present

examples.en: The risk of earthquakes is ever-present everywhere.
The possibility of accidents is always there, so be careful.

examples.ko: 두 나라 사이에는 갈등이 상존하고 있어요.
examples.en: Conflict constantly exists between the two countries.
Even though the danger was always there, nobody knew.

examples.ko: 문제가 상존하는 한 불안은 사라지지 않아요.
examples.en: As long as the problem persists, the anxiety won't go away.
Even a small risk should be prepared for if it's always present.

explain: 위험, 문제, 갈등처럼 좋지 않은 것이 늘 있을 때 주로 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '늘 있다'라고 하고, '상존하다'는 뉴스나 글에서 더 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: There are constant dangers at sea, so please be careful.
phrases.nuance_ko: '상존하다'를 명사 앞에 붙인 형태로, 늘 있는 위험이나 문제를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form, used for dangers or problems that are always present.

phrases.example: 두 나라 사이에 갈등이 아직도 상존하고 있어요.
phrases.en: Conflict still remains between the two countries.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금도 계속 남아 있다는 뜻으로 뉴스나 글에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it still continues to exist; common in news and writing.

phrases.example: 집 안에도 작은 사고의 위험이 늘 있어요.
phrases.en: There is always a risk of small accidents even at home.
phrases.nuance_ko: '상존하다'의 쉬운 말로, 일상 대화에서 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday way to say '상존하다' in conversation.

explain_en: Formal, risks or problems that are constantly present (위험이 상존하다) It is mostly used for unwelcome things like risks, problems, or conflicts that are always present. In daily talk people say '늘 있다', while '상존하다' appears more in news and writing.

t90.ax: The risk of earthquakes is ever-present everywhere.

examples.en: Korea and Vietnam established diplomatic relations in 1992.

examples.ko: 수교 삼십 주년을 기념하는 행사가 열렸어요.
examples.en: An event marking the thirtieth anniversary of diplomatic ties was held.

examples.ko: 두 나라는 수교 이후 교류가 크게 늘었어요.
examples.en: Since establishing relations, exchanges between the two countries have grown a lot.
The number of countries with diplomatic ties grew gradually.
We learned about the process of establishing relations in history class.
Thanks to diplomatic relations, flight routes were also created.

explain: 수교는 나라와 나라가 정식으로 외교 관계를 맺는 거예요. 보통 '수교하다', '수교를 맺다'로 쓰고, 한국과 다른 나라의 사이를 말할 때 '수교 몇 주년'이라고 해요. 관계를 끊는 건 '단교'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The two countries established diplomatic relations long ago.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수교하다'와 같은 뜻이고, 관계를 '맺는다'고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 수교하다, saying the relationship is 'formed'.

phrases.example: 수교 이후 두 나라 사이의 여행이 늘었어요.
phrases.en: Since the establishment of relations, travel between the two countries has increased.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수교한 때부터 지금까지를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the period from when relations began until now.

phrases.en: The two countries formally establish relations this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '수교'에 '-하다'를 붙인 동사형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form made by adding -하다 to the noun 수교.

explain_en: The act of starting official relations (수교 30주년) 수교 is two countries formally starting diplomatic relations. It is usually used as 수교하다 or 수교를 맺다, and anniversaries are called 수교 몇 주년. Cutting those ties is called 단교.

en: to be composed; to be refined

examples.ko: 친구에게 빌린 돈도 엄연한 빚이니까 약속한 날에 갚아야 해요.
examples.en: Money borrowed from a friend is still a real debt, so you must repay it on the promised day.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 작아도 엄연히 정식 회사예요.
examples.en: This shop is small, but it is undeniably a proper company.

examples.ko: 두 사람의 실력에는 엄연한 차이가 있어요.
examples.en: There is a clear difference in skill between the two of them.

examples.ko: 엄연히 규칙이 있는데도 지키지 않는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Even though there is clearly a rule, many people don't follow it.
No matter how much you deny it, that is a plain fact.

examples.ko: 저는 엄연히 성인인데 아직도 아이 취급을 받아요.
examples.en: I am very much an adult, yet I'm still treated like a child.

explain: 부정하기 어려울 만큼 분명하게 있다는 느낌이에요. 주로 '엄연한 사실/현실/차이', '엄연히'의 모양으로 쓰고, 말할 때는 '엄연히 ~인데요'처럼 상대 말에 반박할 때 잘 나와요.

phrases.example: 그가 거짓말을 한 것은 엄연한 사실이에요.
phrases.en: It is an undeniable fact that he lied.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정할 수 없이 분명한 일을 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for something clear and undeniable.

phrases.en: This is clearly my seat, you know.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대 말에 반박할 때 '엄연히 ~인데요'처럼 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to push back, as in '엄연히 ~인데요'.

phrases.example: 비슷해 보여도 두 말에는 엄연한 차이가 있어요.
phrases.en: Even though they look alike, there is a clear difference between the two words.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷해 보이는 것 사이에 분명한 차이가 있다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say there is a real difference between things that seem alike.

explain_en: It carries the feeling that something clearly exists and is hard to deny. It appears mostly as '엄연한 사실/현실/차이' or '엄연히', and in speech it often shows up when pushing back, as in '엄연히 ~인데요'.

t90.ax: No matter how much you deny it, that is a plain fact.

en: to oust; to expel; to drive out

examples.en: The assembly ousted its leader from his position.
Citizens demanded that the corrupt politician be driven out.
The shareholders held a meeting to oust the president.

examples.ko: 그 단체는 규칙을 어긴 회원을 축출하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The group decided to expel the member who broke the rules.

examples.ko: 침입한 세력을 나라에서 축출하는 데 성공했어요.
examples.en: They succeeded in driving the invading force out of the country.

examples.ko: 반대파를 축출한 뒤 그는 혼자 권력을 잡았어요.
examples.en: After ousting the opposition, he took power alone.

explain: '쫓아내다'나 '내쫓다'를 더 딱딱하게 한 말이에요. 뉴스나 역사에서 권력자, 정치 세력, 조직의 구성원을 내보낼 때 주로 써요. '권좌에서 축출하다'처럼 자리나 장소를 같이 말해요.

phrases.en: The owner kicked the noisy customer out of the shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: '축출하다'를 쉬운 말로 바꾼 표현이에요. 일상에서 널리 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plain-language version of 축출하다, widely used in daily life.
phrases.en_equiv: to drive out; to kick out

phrases.en: That politician was eventually expelled from the party.
phrases.nuance_ko: '축출하다'의 피동 표현으로, 쫓겨나는 쪽을 주어로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, used when the person being expelled is the subject.

phrases.en: The crowd ousted the dictator from power.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높은 권력의 자리에서 사람을 내보낸다는 뜻으로 뉴스나 역사에서 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means removing someone from a seat of power; appears in news and history.

explain_en: It is a stiffer version of '쫓아내다' or '내쫓다'. It is mostly used in news and history for removing a ruler, political force or organization member. It is often paired with a position or place, as in '권좌에서 축출하다'.
